solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Conservative madman fights to see liberal speakers

definitions.note: speakers who are liberal with their words, i.e. talk a lot; plural like the answer

parts.note: a hatter, as in 'mad as a hatter', is a madman
boxes means fights with the fists

explanation.surface: A Tory lunatic brawls to get a hearing from left-leaning orators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks political after 'Conservative', but here it means generous: people who are generous with their talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Compulsive talkers are lavish, or liberal, with words, which is exactly what the plural noun describes.

clue.text: Rivers surround highest part of Edinburgh: Arthur's seat

indicators.note: surround means the two rivers go round the letter taken from the city

parts.note: the Cam (in Cambridge) and the Lot (in France) are two rivers

indicators.note: in a down entry the highest part of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Arthur's Seat is the hill in Edinburgh, so rivers ringing the city's high point sounds like geography.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur's Seat is a real hill overlooking Edinburgh, which makes the definition look like a place in that city; it is King Arthur's court instead.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur held court at the legendary castle, so it was literally the seat of his rule.

clue.text: Pantomime boy involved in a racket

indicators.note: involved in means the boy is wrapped up inside the noise

parts.note: a din is a racket, a loud noise
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A young lad of the stage caught up in a scam or a noisy uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pantomime boy' reads as one phrase, but only 'Pantomime' defines: the show is named after its hero. A pantomime is a traditional British Christmas stage show for families.
explanation.definitionFit: The story of the lad and the magic lamp is one of the best-known Christmas pantomime titles.

clue.text: Fashionable fellow to carry stuffed toy

parts.note: a Teddy, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s youth in Edwardian-style fashion
to bear is to carry

explanation.surface: A dandy is made to lug around a cuddly toy.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths who dressed in Edwardian-style long jackets and drainpipe trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: The plush bear named after Theodore Roosevelt is the classic soft, filled children's toy.

clue.text: Look around park on initially chilly evening

parts.note: a rec, short for recreation ground, is a public park

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Someone takes a stroll round the park one cold evening.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec is British usage for a recreation ground, a local public park or playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal for reconnaissance, a scouting survey of an area, used as a verb meaning to explore.

clue.text: Instrument from old motor in top of aeroplane

parts.note: a motor is a car

indicators.note: in a down entry the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A musical instrument found in a vintage car up in the nose of a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: This small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes is a member of the flute family.

clue.text: Take papa off sugary sweet medicine

indicators.note: take ... off means remove the named letter from the sweet
together with take, signals removing a letter

parts.note: a pear drop is a boiled sugary sweet with a pear flavour
Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Instructions to swap a sugary sweet for proper medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: A pear drop is a British hard-boiled sweet, pear-shaped and flavoured with pear essence.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid treatment dropped into the ear is a medicine for ear complaints.

clue.text: Unmarried lady to celebrate wildly, snaring husband

indicators.note: snaring means the jumbled letters catch the extra letter inside them
wildly signals that the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A single woman about to party hard, catching herself a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is part of the fodder, not a link word: without it the letters fall two short.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is mainly American for a young single woman, especially one at her hen party.

clue.text: Military group drops unknown flotation device

indicators.note: drops means the musicians lose a letter

parts.note: an army band is a military group of musicians
Y is an algebraic unknown, like x and z

explanation.surface: A regimental band lets go of a mysterious buoyancy aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Children learning to swim wear inflatable bands on their upper arms to stay afloat.

clue.text: Irritation of King George, trapped by succession

indicators.note: trapped by means the royal letters sit inside the succession

parts.note: a chain is a succession of linked things
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A monarch's vexation at being bound by the line of succession.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means vexation or annoyance at a disappointment or humiliation.

clue.text: Talking about the stars has reputation diminishing

parts.note: a name is a reputation, as in 'make a name for yourself'
dropping means falling or diminishing

explanation.surface: Gossip about celebrities is making someone's standing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Casually mentioning famous acquaintances to impress others is talking about celebrities, the stars.

clue.text: Leave boy with daughter, hiding in the grass

indicators.note: hiding in means boy and daughter are concealed inside the grass

parts.note: hay is cut and dried grass
Alf is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Leave the lad and his daughter hiding in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' reads as a verb ordering someone off, but it is a noun: time off granted from work.
explanation.definitionFit: A short break from work, taken for only the morning or afternoon, is a form of leave.

clue.text: Saying little, ultimately, when chased by farm animals

indicators.note: chased by means the letter is followed, in the answer, by the animals
ultimately means take the final letter of the word little

parts.note: a pig and a ram are farm animals

explanation.surface: A tiny remark, made while being pursued by livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A pithy, witty remark or maxim is a short saying.

clue.text: Old tongue preserved in gelatine

indicators.note: preserved in means the letters are kept inside the word gelatine

explanation.surface: An ancient language kept in jelly, like a fossil in amber.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of ancient Rome is a classical language no longer spoken natively.

clue.text: Fascinated by dapper new criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are bent out of shape, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Enthralled by a smartly dressed new crook.
explanation.definitionFit: To be absorbed or engrossed in something is to be wrapped up in it, captivated.

clue.text: German forces arrange the march west

indicators.note: arrange means the letters of 'the march' are reordered

explanation.surface: An instruction to organise a march heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: W, written last in the clue, opens the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the name of the combined armed forces of Nazi Germany from 1935 to 1945.

clue.text: Rather agitated, holding live element

indicators.note: holding means the jumbled letters contain the verb
agitated means the letters of rather are stirred up

parts.note: are, as in 'we are', means exist or live

explanation.surface: Rather worked up while keeping a live wire in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live' is the verb (to exist), not the adjective it seems beside 'element'.
explanation.definitionFit: The lanthanides and similar metals are each called a rare earth, a kind of chemical element.

clue.text: Need disheartened reggae singers on the radio

indicators.note: disheartened means remove all the middle of reggae, keeping its outside letters
on the radio means a word is given by how it sounds when broadcast

parts.note: a choir is a group of singers

explanation.surface: A craving for downhearted reggae vocalists on air.
explanation.walkthrough: QUIRE, a set of sheets of paper, is pronounced like CHOIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To require something is to have a need for it; both are verbs.

clue.text: Take me up and away from crazy region in the Middle East

indicators.note: take ... up, in a down entry, means lift the word me so it reads bottom to top
with take, says the word me is turned round in this down entry

parts.note: crazy, as in mad, can mean furious, irate

explanation.surface: A plea to be whisked off up and away from a mad part of the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger was unconvinced too: EM (me going up) plus IRATE for 'crazy', with 'and away from' left as loose linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: A state ruled by an emir, such as Dubai or Qatar, is a territory of the Gulf region.

clue.text: City starts to construct an international relations office

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A city begins building an office for foreign relations.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian capital on the Nile is a major city.

clue.text: Artwork, huge, lacking centrepiece: pass over that

indicators.note: over that means, in a down entry, the pass is placed above the rest

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: lacking centrepiece means the middle letter of the synonym for huge is dropped

parts.note: large means huge

explanation.surface: A huge artwork missing its central panel, so skip it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking centrepiece' takes R from LARGE, leaving LAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture made by sticking assorted pieces of paper or fabric onto a backing is a kind of artwork.

clue.text: What you must do before you expire?

definitions.text: What you must do before you expire?

parts.words: What you must do before you expire?
parts.note: expire literally means breathe out, and you have to breathe in first; the surface sense is dying

explanation.surface: A deathbed bucket list: what to do before you die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expire' suggests dying, but literally it means breathing out, which you can only do after breathing in.
explanation.definitionFit: In its literal sense the word means to draw breath into the lungs, the step before exhaling.

clue.text: Drink quite a large shot

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are broken up

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Ordering a big measure of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a measure of spirits, but it means shot to pieces: the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mexican spirit distilled from agave is an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Like The Woman in White

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
hen is slang for a woman

explanation.surface: A comparison with the Wilkie Collins novel The Woman in White.
explanation.walkthrough: The Woman in White is a Victorian mystery novel by Wilkie Collins; here 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A face drained of colour from shock is pale, as grey-white as cinders.

clue.text: Coward exploits short operation

parts.note: to milk something is to exploit it
op is short for operation

explanation.surface: A coward takes advantage of a brief surgical procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak, timid, spineless person is a wimp, a coward.

clue.text: A grave message?

parts.note: grave seems to mean serious, but the message is carved on a grave

explanation.surface: A serious communication of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' reads as solemn, but it is the tomb where the words are inscribed.
explanation.definitionFit: Words inscribed on a tombstone in memory of the dead are a message on a grave.

clue.text: Tribe besieging city produces trumpet

indicators.note: besieging means the tribe surrounds the city

parts.note: a clan is a tribe
Rio de Janeiro, a Brazilian city, is often called Rio

explanation.surface: A tribe laying siege to a city sounds the trumpet.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a shrill medieval brass instrument, a kind of trumpet used in war.

clue.text: Horribly under the weather, heads off to various places

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters are left in an awful mess, rearranged
heads off means each of the three words loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Feeling dreadfully ill, people set off in all directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads off' leaves NDER HE EATHER; 'Horribly' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in or to scattered locations, all over the place.
